data.exact_reserve_text: Included within net claims incurred of $225,755,000 (2016: $142,768,000) is a deterioration of $5,582,000 in claims reserves established at the prior year (2016: release $3,362,000).

prior_year_events.impact_description: 2016 calendar year higher than expected weather related events including Hurricane Matthew resulted in increased losses that affected policies on risk in that year and impacted development of prior years' reserves.

named_events.event_name: Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria and two Mexican earthquakes
named_events.loss_description: The total net cost of these five events for the 2017 calendar year is $68.8m.
Hurricane Matthew and a number of flood and hail losses in 2016 increased loss experience for the 2016 account.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate opened 2017 with gross claims outstanding of $230.962m (at 1 Jan 2017). During 2017 there was an adverse prior-year reserve movement (deterioration) of $5.582m, reflecting adverse development primarily driven by severe natural catastrophe events (notably hurricanes and earthquakes) and large loss development in property portfolios. The 2017 third-quarter catastrophes (Harvey, Irma, Maria and two Mexican earthquakes) were the principal drivers of net losses in 2017 (total net cost ~$68.8m), with property classes most affected. Non-marine casualty lines performed positively, partially offsetting property deterioration.
